chunks: And ʿĀṣim narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who commits zina while he has not consummated marriage with his wife: is he considered muḥṣan? He said: "No, and not with a bondwoman either."

key_terms.أَ يُحْصَنُ: is he deemed muḥṣan, legally protected through qualifying marriage
key_terms.بِأَهْلِهِ: with his wife; meaning lawful spouse in this context
key_terms.بِالْأَمَةِ: through a bondwoman; a female slave-concubine

ai.seo_question: When is a man considered muḥṣan in the legal rulings of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on iḥṣān in the law of zina. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that a man is not considered muḥṣan if he has not consummated marriage with his wife, and iḥṣān is likewise not established through a bondwoman.
